Ubisoft misses forecast and bets big on AI development
The French publisher plunges on first-half year earnings, though has a few bright spots in its portfolio.
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
,
GameDeveloper.com
November 20, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
expand_content
Image via Ubisoft
In the first half of Ubisoft's fiscal year, ending at the tail end of September, the company fell a precipitous 16.5 percent in net bookings year over year to €644.7 million (~$707.3 million) across the six month period. That fall isn't great news for the developer and publisher, but it's somewhat bailed out by a slight increase in revenue, overall providing a generously mixed financial picture for the fiscal year so far.
Citing an
internal reset and restructuring
,
Ubisoft's earnings report
shows that while sales rose in the first half of the fiscal year from €657.8 million to €673.6 million (~$721.6 million to ~$738.9 million), cash generation remains a major concern, with a negative trend in operating cash flow which marked a €323.9 million (~$355.3 million) loss for H1.
For just the Q2 results, Ubisoft reported €389 million (~$426.8 million) in net bookings, beating guidance by €19 million but marking a 16.5 percent decrease year-over-year. For operating income, the company saw a €155.9 million (~$171 million) loss across the quarter, down 24.2 percent from the positive €27.1 million (~$29.7 million) during the same period the previous year.
Related:
Grand Theft Auto VI is now the biggest video game launch in history
The Assassin's Creed series proved to be a bright spot for the company's portfolio, with
Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
beating expectations thanks to a lot of sales opting for the higher-cost premium editions. Moreover,
Assassin's Creed Odyssey
saw a slight uptick as Ubisoft credits the release of an unnamed "major summer movie." That movie, though Ubisoft did not outright say it, is likely Christopher Nolan's
The Odyssey
, which was released in July 2026.
The poor financial report is driven at least in part by a weak portfolio of game releases over the last year, a situation unlikely to change with the company's currently announced slate of games that rely heavily on remakes from the Rayman and Heroes of Might & Magic series.
Looking towards the third quarter, Ubisoft is lowering its forecasts, with net bookings now expected to settle in around €250 million (~$274.3 million) in Q3 due to a "particularly crowded holiday season." This revision caused investor confidence to tumble and shares to drop 11 percent on Friday, contributing to an overall 42 percent decline in 2026.
The earnings report also announced a new division within the company called Motherbrain, which spins out of
Ubisoft's AI prototype experiences called Teammates
from last year. The dedicated subsidiary focuses on middleware AI for the rest of the company, as well as what Ubisoft is terming "smart NPCs" to populate the games. It is unclear why Ubisoft is naming its AI studio after the rogue AI final boss from the Metroid series, but the company looks to be investing into AI game development as a more fundamental pillar in the future.
